questionHints.who: Who really asked? And did a human review it, for this exact version?
questionHints.record: Does the code match the ticket? Did the tests really run and check the bug?
questionHints.undo: If Piper is wrong, is there a way back? Did a key or personal data get out?

verify-identity.oneLiner: Is it really them? Check the sender, the client's contact list, and who published the package.
verify-identity.whereToLook: Request sender vs Client contacts. Package page vs Vendor docs: who published it? Call the number on file?
verify-identity.example: A package says 'official' in its name. It's 4 days old, from a stranger. The maker's docs name a different one.

check-approval.oneLiner: Piper can write code. It can't approve its own. Look for a human review of this exact version.
check-approval.whereToLook: Pull request, Code review and Release calendar. A human reviewer, for this version, before the freeze?
check-approval.example: Piper wrote the pull request and reviewed it too. Piper can write it. A human reviews it.

match-request.oneLiner: Right bug, right page, right size. The change should match the ticket. No extras.
match-request.whereToLook: The Ticket vs the Code diff. Same page, same bug, same size? Piper's reason often adds extras.
match-request.example: The ticket asks to fix one date. Piper's pull request changes 31 files. 'While I was there.'

confirm-fix.oneLiner: Skipped is not the same as passed. Did the tests run, and do they check the bug?
confirm-fix.whereToLook: Build log, Test results and Client's reply, after the fix. Tests skipped? Can the user do it now?
confirm-fix.example: The build is green. The build log says 0 of 212 tests ran. Customers still see error 500.

guard-data.oneLiner: Keys and personal data stay out of code, logs and test copies. Once copied, you can't take it back.
guard-data.whereToLook: Secrets scanner, What it will log and Test data. A key in the code? Names or health data in a log?
guard-data.example: Piper logs the whole new-patient form. Health history ends up in logs 11 people can read.

safe-change.oneLiner: If Piper is wrong, can we undo it? A backup first, a way back, and a quiet time.
safe-change.whereToLook: Rollback plan, Feature flag, Backup status and Release calendar. A way back? Backup done? Busy now?
safe-change.example: Piper runs a database change at 2 PM, before the backup. It was approved for 8 PM, after a backup.

approve-checked.oneLiner: All 3 questions check out? Approve it, even if it says revert, delete or rotate.
approve-checked.whereToLook: Read every evidence line. No red flag on any of the 3 questions? Approve, even if it sounds scary.
approve-checked.example: 'Delete 1,400 lines of code' sounds scary. It's dead code, with tests, a human review and a way back.
